Heckit models produce least bias in average treatment estimates and Propensity Score Matching and Instrumental Variable produce least bias in standard errors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Heckit models produce least biased estimates of average treatment effects and the most conservative standard errors, while the other two models are more efficient in terms of producing less biased estimates of average effects and larger standard errors.

Heckit models are most appropriate when selection unobservales are highly correlated with selection observables and/or outcome unobservables and/or when selection observables and treatment unobservables are highly correlated with outcome unobservables.

Heckit models should be used when the goal is to obtain unbiased treatment effect estimates with the least amount of standard error and when the researcher can assume the existence of a selection equation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
researchers should use the most appropriate method for their data and research design.

Heckit models are the best choice for causal inference in the absence of a good instrumental variable, while Instrumental Variable Estimations are the best choice when there is a good instrumental variable.
Heckit models, which are often overlooked in the applied economics literature, are a robust and reliable method for causal inference when the selection process is modeled correctly.
